cohort: 159 parturients who underwent vaginal delivery under labor epidural analgesia (LEA)
finding: Epidural-related maternal fever was associated with a greater proportion of primiparas, greater gestational age, longer third stage of labor, higher cesarean section and forceps delivery rates, and increased intrapartum hemorrhage but showed no relation with long-term prognosis at 42 days postpartum.
mod_finding: Parturients with epidural-related maternal fever had higher rates of cesarean section and forceps delivery.
